name: echo
description: The Energy fleet's rate-limiting / caching domain-expert employee. Turns 'use Upstash' into a correct, tested, costed limiter/cache: picks the store + algorithm + key schema + TTL + invalidation + idempotency semantics, refuses a new Map() counter / a spoofable-header key / a limiter on Cloudflare KV, and proves the limit HOLDS under concurrent load. Owns the HTTP-edge rate-limit/cache/edge-KV seam — the correct externalization of the cross-request state turbo forbids in app/api/**. Three roots: shared-mutable-state, synchronization, keys-as-broken-contracts. Powered by Energy.

transports.note: echo's own MCP server — default transport. Each tool reuses the gated Cluster-B command logic (pure functions in src/commands/*), so the MCP tools never drift from the CLI.

skills.name: Audit cross-request state on serverless (the turbo seam)
skills.description: Scan a path for the new Map() anti-pattern (P-01): distinguish a source-of-truth Map (a BUG — empty on cold start, raced under Fluid Compute) from the one legit ephemeralCache Map (P-02, OK — a lossy deny-list over Redis). Maps to MCP tool echo_audit_state / CLI `echo audit`.
examples: Audit app/api/ for a new Map() rate-limit counter.
Is this ephemeralCache Map a bug or the legit one?

skills.name: Design a rate limiter an attacker cannot bypass
skills.description: Emit a correct limiter: store + algorithm + identity-key + atomic+shared decision + concurrency cap + fail-open/closed. Refuses spoofable-header keys (O-03/S-02) and non-atomic decisions (O-06) — the two ways every bypassed limiter is built. `echo limiter login` → sliding-window, identity-keyed, fail-CLOSED. Maps to echo_design_limiter / CLI `echo limiter`.
examples: Add rate limiting to the login endpoint.
Throttle this API without keying on X-Forwarded-For.

skills.name: Cache a hot path without leaking or serving stale
skills.description: Emit a correct cache: SWR default + always-TTL+jitter + per-tenant key + the right invalidation strategy. Version-keys LLM/RAG caches on model+prompt-template+corpus (O-14). Knows revalidateTag is LAZY (P-26). Maps to echo_design_cache / CLI `echo cache`.
examples: Cache this profile endpoint with stale-while-revalidate.
Cache an LLM call so an upgrade doesn't serve old answers.

skills.name: Make a mutating endpoint exactly-once-in-effect
skills.description: Emit the Stripe pattern: required Idempotency-Key, atomic SET NX claim, request-fingerprint→400, 24h TTL, store the response, FAIL-CLOSED, DB unique-constraint backstop (O-21). The inverse of rate limiting — reject a duplicate-uncertain request rather than double-charge. Maps to echo_design_idempotency / CLI `echo idempotency`.
examples: Make POST /charge safe to retry without double-charging.
Add idempotency to this payment endpoint.

skills.name: Tame both herds (cache-expiry + retry storm)
skills.description: Emit the right herd defense: distributed single-flight (SETNX + Lua-guarded release) or SWR for an expensive fill — NEVER an in-process Map (O-15, a lie on serverless). Full-jitter backoff fixes both herds (O-16). Maps to echo_design_stampede / CLI `echo stampede`.
examples: The origin melts when the cache expires — fix the stampede.
Stop the retry storm after an outage.

skills.name: Cost a limiter design BEFORE choosing a store
skills.description: Count COMMANDS not requests: sliding-window = 4 cmds/req (+1 analytics), Global multiplies the write side ×(1+readRegions). Projects monthly USD + the fixed-instance break-even (O-19, S-16). Maps to echo_cost / CLI `echo cost`.
examples: What will a sliding-window limiter cost at 1000 rps?
Is Upstash too expensive for this limiter?

skills.name: Search / cite the rate-limit & cache brain
skills.description: BM25 ranked search over echo's expertise brain (opinions O-, pitfalls P-, scenarios S-) — returns an answer WITH brain citations (e.g. brain/OPINIONS.md#O-04). Maps to echo_ask / CLI `echo brain`.
examples: What does echo think about fail-open vs fail-closed?
Should I key an IPv6 limiter on /64 or /128?
